Advertisement View all journals Saved research Search Account Log in Content Explore content About the journal Publish with us Subscribe Sign up for alerts RSS feed nature nature water articles article Article Published: 09 September 2026 Localized potential wells enabling directional electron transport boost photocatalytic uranium extraction from natural seawater Yachao Xu ORCID: orcid.org/0009-0001-7684-9997 1 na1 , Zhong Zhou ORCID: orcid.org/0009-0009-3464-6487 2 , 3 na1 , Ruolan Zhao 4 , Xiaohua Guo 2 , Ying Wang 4 , Youxing Liu ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0003-4407-8785 1 , 2 , Zheng Lin 1 , Zongqiang Sun 1 , Peng Yu 4 , Mingchuan Luo ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0001-9772-2154 1 , Jun Wang ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-7437-8503 5 & … Shaojun Guo ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-5941-414X 1 Show authors Nature Water ( 2026 ) Cite this article Save article View saved research 73 Accesses Metrics details Abstract The directional induction of photoelectron transport to atomic active sites is critical for boosting photocatalytic uranium extraction; however, achieving such tuning remains a grand challenge. Here we report a localized potential well engineering strategy that facilitates the directional injection of photogenerated electrons towards the atomic active sites, which enhance photocatalytic uranium extraction from natural seawater. The as-made industrial-level TAPT–DFBP covalent organic frameworks (COFs) (TAPT: 1,3,5-tris-(4-aminophenyl)triazine, DFBP: 5,5′-diformyl-2,2′-bipyridine) exhibits an average uranium extraction rate of 7.25 mg g −1 d −1 , which is higher than those of reported active materials. The as-fabricated large-area TAPT–DFBP COF film (150 cm × 250 cm) possesses a high photocatalytic uranium extraction capacity of 8.9 mg g −1 from real marine environments. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the construction of localized potential wells within COFs induce multiple electron transport paths towards atomic active sites, thereby facilitating the separation of photogenerated electron–hole pairs and enhancing the photocatalytic uranium extraction from natural seawater.
